title: cross-functional-roadmap-sync-prep-mar-2026-ryan-scratchpad
content:
Meeting: Cross-functional roadmap alignment (Product + Eng + Applied ML)
Date: 2026-03-12 10:00am PT (30-45m)
Owner/Prep: Ryan Chen (taking notes)
Attendees (ask to confirm): Maya (Product PM - Hosted API), Asha (Product - Optimize), Raj (Eng - Serving Runtime), Lina (Applied ML), John (Infra lead?) TBD

Purpose / desired outcomes:
- Surface blockers that could shift Q2 roadmap (deployments, perf, infra costs)
- Confirm model rollout cadence and gating criteria for hosted vs dedicated vs private launches
- Align on evaluation / quality gating (evals, smoke tests, perf targets)
- Capture action items and owners for next 2 weeks

Background (short):
- Product proposed aggressive model upgrades for hosted catalog (2 major model families) with staggered canaries across regions.
- Eng (Raj) flagged potential perf regressions on 8k context for one model variant; needs kernel tuning + additional perf tests.
- Applied ML (Lina) running quality evals; saw slight regressions on few LLM tasks (few-shot summarization) when quantized to 4-bit profile.
- Dedicated/private customers expressed interest in earlier access but require SLA/throughput numbers and security checklist.

Agenda (20-30m):
1) Quick round (2m) - attendees + one-line top concern
2) Product outline of proposed rollouts & timing (5m) - Maya/Asha
3) Eng perf status & immediate blockers (5m) - Raj
4) Applied ML quality findings + suggested mitigations (5m) - Lina
5) Risk triage & tradeoffs (5m) - open discussion
6) Action items + owners + deadlines (3m)

Key talking points / prompts I want to raise:
- Maya: do we have hard dates or just target quarters for each model? Are customers already committed to specific timelines?
- Raj: can you summarize the perf regression repro steps and where you need support (bench infra, more traces, sample prompts)? Is a hotfix kernel plausible before canary?
- Lina: which evaluation sets showed regressions and can we isolate whether it's quantization or tokenizer differences? Any quick A/B test we can run during canary?
- For Dedicated/Private: what are the minimum throughput numbers we can guarantee without overloaded buffer -> are there contingency plans (fallback model)?
- Contention w/ infra budget: if we need additional GPU pool for canaries, what's the rough cost estimate and lead time?

Notes / quick scribbles (informal):
- Raj said "8k context + kv cache mishandling" - need to confirm whether it's OOM or latency spike.
- Lina: 4-bit profile seems to cause subtle coherence drop on long summaries; might be dataset-specific. Ask for examples.
- Maya: customers on Dedicated want earlier preview; could offer "preview cohort" with NDA + usage cap. Good sales/CS ask.
- John's availability uncertain next week (infra capacity planning) -> ask Arjun as backup?

Risks and mitigation brainstorm (short):
- Risk: Perf regression causes canary rollback and delays rollout. Mitigation: schedule extra perf CI, smaller canary %, pre-warm KV caches, fallback variant (non-quantized) ready.
- Risk: Quality regressions leak to customer-facing endpoints. Mitigation: gated eval thresholds, canary on internal customers first, manual review for N days.
- Risk: Dedicated customers demand earlier access -> conflict with hosted stability. Mitigation: separate preview plane (isolated pool) + documented SLA expectations.

Proposed gating criteria (to propose in meeting):
- Latency P95 within X% of baseline (quantify during meeting; propose 20% initially)
- Token cost delta acceptable (product to weigh)
- Eval pass rate: >95% on core prompt suite (Lina to supply current pass rate and failing cases)
- No showstopper infra issues (OOMs, thread-safety) in 72h perf smoke tests

Action items (capture here so I can paste to meeting notes quickly):
- Raj: reproduce perf regression with minimal repro script + post perf traces to GH issue by 2026-03-15 (owner: Raj) [due 2026-03-15]
- Lina: share failing eval examples + suggested mitigations (quantization adjustments, alternate tokenizer) by 2026-03-14 (owner: Lina) [due 2026-03-14]
- Maya/Asha: confirm rollout target dates and customer preview candidates by 2026-03-16 (owner: Maya) [due 2026-03-16]
- Ryan: schedule follow-up triage (30m) if perf repro confirmed; invite infra + release eng (owner: Ryan) [tentative 2026-03-17]
- John/Arjun: confirm if we can spin a small isolated GPU pool for preview + rough cost estimate by 2026-03-18 (owner: John/Arjun)

Open questions to close in meeting (or async):
- Exact latency target number (P95) acceptable to product for canary?
- Are there legal/compliance blockers for previewing private deployments to customers?
- If rollback happens, what is the communication plan to customers (who owns messaging)?

Post-meeting plan (how I'll update notes):
- Convert action items to JIRA tasks with owners + due dates
- Link perf repro GH issue and Lina's eval doc in the sync notes
- Follow up with CS on preview cohort list if Maya provides names

Personal prep checklist (before meeting):
- Pull latest perf dashboard snapshots (Grafana links) -> attach to notes
- Open Lina's eval doc and highlight failing prompts (get examples)
- Create one slide for quick context if needed (1 slide)
- Set up recording + take notes for immediate action-item capture

Quick links (to paste during meeting):
- Perf dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-internal/d/serve/perf-overview
- Eval doc (Lina): https://confluence.redwood/inference/evals/q1-2026
- GH issue template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/issues/new/choose

Misc scratchpad (things I might say):
- "Let's prioritize a minimal repro - that will tell us whether it's infra or model-level."
- "If we need to delay hosted rollout, can we at least publish a clear timeline to customers?"
- "Preview cohort + usage cap seems low-friction and buys us time for fixes."
action_items: Raj: reproduce perf regression + post traces to GH issue by 2026-03-15
Lina: share failing eval examples + mitigations by 2026-03-14
Maya/Asha: confirm rollout dates + preview candidates by 2026-03-16
Ryan: schedule follow-up triage + invite infra/release by 2026-03-17
John/Arjun: confirm isolated GPU pool feasibility + cost estimate by 2026-03-18
